title: Does cross-platform play belong inside this multiplayer increment?
summary: This increment already defines the smallest faithful multiplayer slice: one player creates a session, one joins, both share a real-time fixed-tick simulation over WebSocket with solo play intact. The open question is whether those two players must be able to sit on different platforms (e.g., a web client and a native desktop client) within this same increment. Answering yes widens the work: transport and input handling get re-examined under a platform matrix, acceptance gains cross-platform pairings, and the schedule stretches (risk R2). Answering no keeps the increment narrow — and because the adopted defaults (host-authoritative topology, WebSocket behind an abstraction, interface-isolated sync strategy) are deliberately platform-neutral, cross-platform can be added later without a rewrite, especially if a forward-compatibility constraint is recorded now. Either answer settles the boundary: the readiness review blocks authorization precisely because this scope member is currently neither in nor out, so the Definition correctly refused to guess it for you.

options.label: Exclude — deliberate non-goal
options.description: Cross-platform play is recorded as an explicit non-goal of this increment. Only the current single target platform is in scope; platform interoperability is deferred to a future increment with no new constraint attached.

options.label: Exclude, but preserve the option
options.description: Cross-platform stays out of this increment's acceptance, but add a constraint that the transport and input abstractions remain platform-neutral (WebSocket-behind-an-interface, abstracted input) so a later increment can add platforms without rework. Costs a little discipline in the abstraction layer now; no platform matrix or cross-platform test pairings.

options.label: Include minimal cross-platform
options.description: Require the shared session to work across the platforms already reachable by the chosen transport (e.g., the same build running on two different OS/browser combinations). No new native or mobile clients are built; acceptance gains cross-platform pairings and their latency-budget runs.

options.label: Include cross-platform fully
options.description: Make inter-platform play a first-class requirement: at least two genuinely distinct clients (e.g., web and native desktop) interoperating in one shared session. Transport and input choices are re-examined under a platform matrix, acceptance must cover cross-platform pairings end-to-end, and the increment's schedule grows accordingly.
